preApply.protectedScreening: Each record has two immutable full-text include votes, a ready_for_extraction resolution, and a promotion link. No screening-record, vote, resolution, promotion, source-file, or extraction-field write is staged.

checks: Each attached primary PDF was inspected once in full, including every results table and usable figure. The locally inspected SHA-256 value matches papers.primary_file_sha256 for all three records.
No paper has a compatible Tabs 1-10 injury or illness-surveillance payload, so no population layout or extraction field is staged. Structured-population dual writing is therefore not applicable.

S4716 is a Spanish youth-soccer competitive-anxiety study. Its sole injury measure is a season-long total injury count used in descriptive/correlational anxiety analyses; the paper reports no at-risk denominator, injury type, injury severity, location, mechanism, illness outcome, or compatible surveillance measure. Its existing mental_health status is retained rather than forcing a sparse extraction.

S5428 is a cross-sectional DASS-21 study of licensed central and assistant referees, not current football-player participants. All results tables report depression, anxiety, stress, role, league, sex, demographics, and regression associations; no injury or illness outcome is reported. It is staged for the true referee exclusion status.

S5482 is a nationwide Swedish register cohort of current/former top-division male players. Its outcomes are diagnosed depression/anxiety-related disorders and suicide; Tables 1-5 and Figure 1-2 contain registry, demographic, mental-health, suicide, and hazard-ratio results only. Its existing mental_health status is retained.

classifications.caveat: Although the study prospectively tracks a season total of injuries, it is an anxiety-risk-factor study and supplies only an injury-count distribution without a usable injury-surveillance denominator or compatible Tabs 1-10 outcome detail.
